key_insight: Competing Ge-driven polar off-centering and Sn-favored octahedral tilting create a low-temperature morphotropic phase boundary at x = 0.60–0.65 in CsGe₁₋ₓSnₓBr₃.
engineering_relevance: Ge/Sn mixing offers a route to tune polar order, crystal symmetry, and band gaps in lead-free halide perovskites.
method: Train a charge-aware machine-learned interatomic potential on hybrid-functional data.
Run large-scale molecular dynamics across the full Ge/Sn composition range.
Map structural phases and composition- and temperature-dependent band gaps.
evidence_signal: The simulated phase diagram reproduces known transition sequences and temperatures of both end members and predicts an intermediate tetragonal I4/mcm phase near the boundary.
watch_item: The predicted alloy phase boundary and intermediate phase require experimental validation beyond agreement with the end members.
paper_title: Competing Octahedral Tilting and $B$-Site Off-Centering Govern the Phase Diagram of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ Perovskite Alloys
